Waubonsee Community College is a public community college with four campuses in Illinois: the main campus in Sugar Grove, two campuses in Aurora (Aurora Downtown and Aurora Fox Valley, formerly known as the Copley Campus), and one in Plano.

[edit | edit source]
Founded in August 1966, Waubonsee Community College began shaping its infrastructure and curriculum in early 1967. To name the new institution, the college organized a district-wide contest. "Waubonsee," meaning "early dawn" or "early day," was chosen, honoring Chief Waubonsie, a Potawatomi chief who lived in the Fox River Valley in the 1800s.[3]

[edit | edit source]
The college initially held classes at community facilities in September 1967, serving 1,603 students. A successful bond referendum in December 1967 facilitated the establishment of a permanent campus, which opened in Sugar Grove on a 243-acre site. This main campus has since expanded to include various educational and recreational facilities, including laboratories, a library, and a nature trail.[3]

[edit | edit source]
In 1986, Waubonsee opened a second campus in downtown Aurora, later relocating in 2011 to a new 132,000-square-foot facility on River Street. This campus serves as a hub for adult education and community services, including GED programs, ESL courses, and the Illinois Small Business Development Center.[3]
In January 1997, Waubonsee established the Aurora Fox Valley Campus, next to Copley Medical Center, which houses healthcare programs and offers general education courses. The Plano Campus, opened in 2011, recently evolved into the Innovation and Design Center, featuring programs in computer-aided design, cybersecurity, and welding.[3]
The Learning Academy provides training and support for Illinois community college educators in the development, design and delivery of online courses.
The college also expanded its online offerings, providing nearly 200 courses and full associate degrees online.

value.text:
Waubonsee Community College is a public community college in Illinois, United States. Its campus network includes the main campus in Sugar Grove, Aurora Downtown, Aurora Fox Valley and Plano. The institution takes its name from a district-wide naming contest: Waubonsee was selected in honor of Chief Waubonsie, a Potawatomi chief associated with the Fox River Valley.

Founded in August 1966, the college began developing its infrastructure and curriculum in early 1967. Classes started in community facilities in September of that year. A successful bond referendum in December 1967 supported the establishment of a permanent Sugar Grove campus. The college opened a downtown Aurora campus in 1986 and relocated that campus to River Street in 2011. Aurora Fox Valley was established in January 1997, while the Plano campus opened in 2011.

Academic provision extends beyond the principal campuses through community extension sites and distance learning. Aurora Fox Valley houses healthcare programmes and general education courses. The Plano location developed into an Innovation and Design Center with programmes in computer-aided design, cybersecurity and welding. The college has also expanded online teaching, including full associate degrees, and provides training and support for community college educators through the ILCCO Learning Academy.
